# Generated Audit Artifact

A script emits a report; the report is **committed next to its output**; the claim then points at the
report rather than at prose. Five repositories do this, in four different shapes. It is the strongest
verification habit in the source set and the direct counterweight to
[[documentation-drift]].

## Shape 1 — a dated audit backed by re-runnable checkers

`Optimization Methods` ships `tools/verify_reports.py` and `tools/verify_chromosomes.py`, and commits
`docs/DATA_VERIFICATION.md` stamped "Date of check: 2026-07-09", surfaced as a README badge
(`data checks 36/36 ✓`) with re-run instructions. The checker re-parses all 36 solver reports for
internal consistency **and cross-checks a hard-coded copy of the paper's Table 7 to ±2 m** — so it is
a genuine external check, not a self-check.

> "Re-running the deterministic `greedy` on a freshly downloaded Wrocław graph gave 178,207 /
> 322,318 / 458,921 m vs the paper's 177,555 / 299,944 / 481,089 m — same demands and capacity, but a
> different sampled road graph (OSM has drifted; today's largest SCC = 3,893 nodes)."
> — Optimization Methods/final_project/docs/DATA_VERIFICATION.md, 2026-07-09

A negative reproducibility result, kept.

## Shape 2 — the audit gates the build

`labour-fraud-analysis` is the most developed instance. `make docs` regenerates `docs/schema.md`,
`docs/data-dictionary.md`, `docs/coverage.md` and `data/_counts.json`; CI then runs
`git diff --exit-code` on exactly those four paths, so a stale generated doc **fails the build**. See
[[generated-docs-checked-by-ci-diff]] and [[reproducible-analysis]].

The same repo also shows the limit of the technique. Its README claims "no value here identifies a
real party — a claim that is test-verified in CI", but the workflow says:

> "On a clean runner the private source + rules are absent, so the leak/stem scans skip and this
> enforces structural integrity + the PII regex sweep."
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/.github/workflows/ci.yml, 2026-07-11

The gate is real but narrower than the prose claims. Recorded on [[disclosure-gate]].

## Shape 3 — a reproducible command transcript

`browser_game_stickfps/docs/security-audit-phase7.md` reproduces each `grep`, its literal output, and
what that output proves, plus a named Limitations section — explicitly "reproducible — rerun the same
commands against a later commit to re-verify the invariant". It backs
[[server-authoritative-netcode]].

## Shape 4 — the artefact audits its own generator

`Physics/exam_prep/tools/build_sets.mjs` emits both `js/quizsets.js` and `tools/AUDIT.md`, and the
audit reports numbers that contradict the generator's own header comment (75 bank questions vs a
comment saying 62). The audit is honest about the code that produced it. It also records a
domain-level finding — that two answers in a provided exam key were wrong — see
[[jaccard-similarity-set-selection]].

## Shape 5 — a runtime black box

`Farley`'s diagnostics store is an audit artefact generated by *use* rather than by a build: a
ring-buffered IndexedDB log of eight event kinds, exportable as `farely-diagnostics-YYYY-MM-DD.json`.
See [[on-device-black-box-diagnostics]].

## Where it is absent

`Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories`, `Python-Programming-Laboratories`, `Oracle-Database-Laboratories`
and `Cybersecurity-Engineering-Laboratories` have **no** generated audit. The nearest thing —
`Python-Programming-Laboratories` — actively gitignores its generated output as "all reproducible from
source", which is the opposite choice: trust the generator, don't commit its output.

One instance is a partial: `IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/docs/branch-reports/`
is 846 lines of mechanical per-branch audit of a *different* repository, but its generator was never
committed — so the report cannot be re-run.
